module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1041

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1041](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1041)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial MeasureTheory ENNReal

namespace Erdos1041

section ComponentLemma

variable (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]) (hn : n ≥ 2) (hnum : f.natDegree = n)
variable (h_monic : f.Monic)
variable (h : f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.ball 0 1)
include hn hnum h h_monic

/--
The length of a subset $s$ of $\mathbb{C}$ is defined to be its 1-dimensional
Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(s)$.
-/
noncomputable def length (s : Set ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ := μH[1] s

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Erdős–Herzog–Piranian Component Lemma** (Metric Properties of Polynomials, 1958):
If $f$ is a monic degree $n$ polynomial with all roots in the unit disk,
then some connected component
of $\{z \mid |f(z)| < 1\}$ contains at least two roots with multiplicity.

See p. 139, above Problem 5:
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., _Metric properties of polynomials_.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 32]
theorem exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots :
    ∃ C, C ⊆ {z | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1} ∧ IsConnected C ∧
      2 ≤ (f.roots.filter (· ∈ C)).card := by
  sorry

end ComponentLemma

/--
Let
$$ f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} (z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[x] $$
with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

Conjecture: Must there always exist a path of length less than 2 in
$$ \{ z \in \mathbb{C} \mid |f(z)| < 1 \} $$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?

The answer is negative. ani gave a counterexample of degree seven on the
[Erdős problems forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1041) on 7 September 2026.
The linked formalisation proves, for the member $s = 10^{-6}$ of ani's family, that every
connected subset of $\{ z \mid |f(z)| < 1 \}$ containing two distinct roots has
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure greater than $2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 32, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos/blob/0ee31b3a99ef93d2b679a427b474b23710597bad/lean/ErdosProblems/Erdos1041/Counterexample/HausdorffLength.lean#L449-L454"]
theorem erdos_1041 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]), n ≥ 2 → f.natDegree = n → f.Monic →
      f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.ball 0 1 →
      ∃ (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (h : ({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots) (γ : Path z₁ z₂),
        Set.range γ ⊆ { z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1 } ∧ length (Set.range γ) < 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos1041

reformulations.difference: A path's length is taken to be the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of its image, `μH[1] (Set.range γ)` (via `Erdos1041.length`). The source means the arc length (total variation) of the path γ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two versions agree for each f. Source ⇒ Lean: for any rectifiable path, H¹(γ([0,1])) ≤ length(γ) < 2. Lean ⇒ source: K = γ([0,1]) is a continuum with H¹(K) < 2 < ∞. By the classical theorem (Falconer, Geometry of Fractal Sets, Lemmas 3.2 and 3.12; Ważewski / Eilenberg–Harrold), K contains an arc A from z₁ to z₂. For an arc, length(A) = H¹(A) ≤ H¹(K) < 2, and A ⊆ K ⊆ {|f|<1}. The constant path covers z₁ = z₂ in both versions. Lean checks: `hausdorffMeasure_segment` makes `length` of the segment [0, 1+i] equal √2, and (X−1/2)(X+1/2) satisfies the body via the segment through 0, so the definition is a genuine length. The external development also proves the counterexample in both forms (total variation in Assembly.lean, H¹ in HausdorffLength.lean).

reformulations.difference: "Connects two of the roots" is encoded as `({z₁, z₂} : Multiset ℂ) ≤ f.roots`. So a repeated root, joined to itself by the constant path of H¹-length 0, counts as two roots. A polynomial with a repeated root therefore satisfies the body trivially.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `f.roots` is the multiset {z_1,…,z_n} from the source's factorisation ∏(z−z_i). We have {a,b} ≤ f.roots exactly when a = z_i and b = z_j for some i ≠ j, which is literally "two of the z_i" (EHP58: "joins two of the z_ν"). The erdosproblems.com forum settled this reading (BorisAlexeev, 6 Dec 2025: "for roots with multiplicity, the 0-length path connecting them should count for this problem"). Pendyala (arXiv 2606.24875) uses the same convention: zeros "counted with multiplicity", joined by a "possibly degenerate polygonal path". The answer is negative, so the Lean claim (the negation of the multiset version) also implies the negative answer under a distinct-roots reading. In Lean I checked that X² satisfies the body with `Path.refl 0`, and that a degree-1 polynomial cannot supply {z₁, z₂}.

reformulations.difference: EHP's "one component of E contains at least two zeros" is stated as "there is a connected set C ⊆ {|f|<1} containing at least two roots counted with multiplicity". It does not refer to connected components explicitly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any connected C ⊆ E lies inside `connectedComponentIn E x` for a point x ∈ C, so that component contains at least as many roots. Conversely, the component of any point of E is a nonempty connected subset of E. I proved the `↔` in Lean for arbitrary f using `IsPreconnected.subset_connectedComponentIn`, `Multiset.monotone_filter_right`, `connectedComponentIn_subset` and `isConnected_connectedComponentIn_iff`.

review.notes:
I found no misformalizations in the three declarations.

**`erdos_1041`**
- The statement matches EHP58 Problem 5 on p. 139 ("If all the z_ν lie in D, does there exist a path of length less than 2 which lies in E and joins two of the z_ν?") and erdosproblems.com/1041. It keeps a monic polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 (needed for "two of the roots"), all zeros in the open disk, the strict lemniscate {|f|<1}, the strict bound < 2, the multiplicity reading, and the correct polarity: `answer(False)` means "not always".
- Lean checks rule out a vacuous or trivial body:
  - `length` is a genuine Euclidean length (H¹ of the segment [0, 1+i] is √2).
  - A repeated root is witnessed by `Path.refl`.
  - A one-root polynomial cannot supply `{z₁, z₂} ≤ roots`.
  - (X−1/2)(X+1/2) satisfies the body via the straight segment.

**The linked formal proof**
- I built it against the sandbox's Lean/Mathlib v4.33.1; it targets v4.29.1. This needed only API-drift patches:
  - `LocPathConnectedSpace` → `LocallyPathConnectedSpace`;
  - `Real.sin_bound` now gives a stronger x⁵/100 bound;
  - `Real.sin_gt_sub_cube` no longer takes `x ≤ 1`;
  - an added `import Mathlib` for `Polynomial.hasDerivAt`;
  - a `Subtype.map` simp lemma;
  - `rfl` for instance side goals after `convert`.
- The result depends on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and proves exactly the repository's statement (`fcLength` is `Erdos1041.length` verbatim). I did not build it on its native v4.29.1 toolchain.
- The docstring's description is accurate: s = 10⁻⁶, degree 7, "every connected subset containing two distinct roots has H¹ > 2" (the external lemma says preconnected, which is the same here).

**`exists_connected_component_contains_two_roots`**
- This is EHP's remark directly above Problem 5: "if all zeros of (1) lie in D, then one component of E contains at least two zeros".
- The open disk is essential: zⁿ+1 gives n components when zeros lie on the circle.
- The "p. 139, above Problem 5" citation checks out. I mapped the text object to PDF page 15, and the paper starts on p. 125.

**Metadata nits (not findings)**
- The AMS 32 tag ("several complex variables") is unusual for a one-variable problem; sibling lemniscate files 1043–1048 use AMS 30.
- The docstring writes ℂ[x]; erdosproblems.com corrected this to ℂ[z] on 2025-10-20.
